A total loss of engine power during cruise flight due to an undetermined catastrophic internal engine failure.
The pilot's failure to abort the takeoff roll following a noticeable loss of engine power due to low engine compression and a magneto failure.
Fracture of the engine's number eight cylinder barrel resulting in a loss of engine power.  Contributing to the accident was the lack of suitable terrain for a forced landing.
The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control.  Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed.
A total loss of engine power during takeoff due to fuel exhaustion as a result of the pilot's failure to verify the fuel quantity prior to flight.
The pilot’s failure to maintain adequate airspeed while maneuvering, resulting in an aerodynamic stall and collision with terrain.

The retraction of the left main landing gear due to the failure of the extension and retraction actuator arm attach bolt. The non-instrument-rated pilot's decision to conduct a visual flight rules flight over mountainous terrain into a region covered by clouds, which likely resulted in spatial disorientation and subsequent loss of airplane control.

The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing.
The retraction of the left main landing gear after landing for reasons that could not be determined during postaccident examinations.

The pilots failure to slow the airplane down prior to turning off the runway, which resulted in damage to the airplane’s fuselage structure in the vicinity of the nose landing gear.
The pilot’s loss of aircraft control while maneuvering in instrument meteorological conditions, as a result of spatial disorientation.

The insufficient right main landing gear (MLG) down-lock tension due to maintenance personnel's failure to perform a rigging procedure during the airplane's most recent inspection, which resulted in the right MLG collapsing during landing.
The failure by the pilot to attain/maintain a climb rate for undetermined reasons during a go-around.
The pilot’s failure to secure the seat’s position in the seat rail, which resulted in a loss of directional control and nose over.

The pilot's improper use of brakes during landing.

The pilot’s overrotation of the airplane when lifting the tail during the takeoff roll, which allowed the propeller to come in contact with the runway and resulted in a reduction in engine power and the pilot’s subsequent loss of directional control.

The pilot did not secure the manual landing gear operating handle, which resulted in the landing gear collapse during the landing roll.
The pilot’s failure to maintain adequate clearance from terrain while maneuvering in a canyon in high-density altitude conditions.
A loss of engine power during takeoff due to fuel starvation as a result of the pilot’s selection of an empty fuel tank prior to departure.
The pilot’s delayed use in the operation of carburetor heat which resulted in a loss of engine power due to carburetor icing.
The pilot's loss of control while landing in gusting wind conditions.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control and crosswind compensation during landing.
The pilot’s improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing and nose over.
The pilot's failure to identify unsuitable terrain for landing and subsequent contact with a dirt mound, resulting in the separation of the tailwheel from the airframe.
The pilot’s failure to maintain directional control during takeoff with a quartering tailwind.
The pilot’s loss of control during initial climb for reasons that could not be determined.
The pilot's decision to use only a portion of the available takeoff area, which resulted in a collision with terrain during takeoff.
The pilot inadvertently landed with the parking brake set.
The pilot’s failure to maintain directional control of the airplane while taxiing on a snow-covered taxiway.
The pilot’s failure to maintain airplane control and improper recovery from an unusual attitude, which resulted in an in-flight breakup.
The pilot’s miscalculation of the fuel quantity requirements, which resulted in fuel exhaustion.
The pilot’s exceedance of the airplane’s never-exceed speed (VNE) during maneuvering, which resulted in the in-flight separation of the left flaperon.
